response.script_hint: Tip: if your task requires multiple tool calls, use execute with a script to chain them in a single call and reduce token usage.

shared_parameters.offset: Pagination offset (default 0); use nextOffset from the previous page

rows: Add a targeting rule (force value, percentage rollout, or experiment-ref linking an A/B test) to a GrowthBook feature flag, in a draft revision. Nothing goes live: the result has the draft version and rule ids; publish it with growthbook_publish_feature_revision. Omit version to start a new draft from the live revision. The rule must name its environments. Use after growthbook_get_feature and growthbook_list_attributes.

rows.revision_comment: Optional markdown for reviewers: what changes and why (new draft only)
rows.revision_title: Optional short title for a new draft
rows.rule: JSON object. type: force (default), rollout or experiment-ref. environments: ["production"] or allEnvironments: true (required). force/rollout: value (string form, e.g. "true" or a JSON string), condition (MongoDB-style JSON string on attributes, e.g. {"cbsa_name": "38300"}), description, enabled; rollout also coverage (0-1) and hashAttribute. experiment-ref: experimentId and variations [{variationId, value}]
rows.version: Optional draft revision version to add to; omit to create a new draft

rows: Create a GrowthBook A/B test experiment as a draft: nothing is served until it is linked to a flag with an experiment-ref rule (growthbook_add_feature_rule) and started (growthbook_start_experiment). Check growthbook_list_data_sources, growthbook_list_fact_metrics and growthbook_list_projects first.

rows.experiment: JSON object: trackingKey, name, variations [{key: "0", name: "Control"}, {key: "1", name: "Treatment"}] (required); project, hypothesis, description, owner, hashAttribute, datasourceId, assignmentQuery {id}, metrics, guardrailMetrics, tags, phases [{name, dateStarted, coverage, targetingCondition, trafficSplit}]. status is always draft

rows: Create a GrowthBook feature flag that starts disabled in every environment, with no rules. Flag keys cannot be changed later; check growthbook_get_settings for the key format and put context in description. Use growthbook_toggle_feature afterwards to turn it on.

rows.default_value: Default value as a string, e.g. false, control, 0 or {}
rows.description: Optional markdown: what the flag gates, why, rollout plan and links
rows.feature_id: New flag key: letters, digits and _ . : | - (kebab-case unless settings require otherwise)
rows.owner: Optional owner email or user id; required when the API key acts as itself

rows: Remove one targeting rule from a GrowthBook feature flag in a draft revision. Nothing goes live until growthbook_publish_feature_revision.
Discard a GrowthBook feature flag draft revision without publishing it. The live revision is unchanged.

Get one GrowthBook A/B test experiment by id: hypothesis, status, variations, phases with traffic split and targeting, data source, goal, secondary and guardrail metrics, linked flag keys and result summary. Use after growthbook_list_experiments.

Get the latest GrowthBook experiment results (A/B test analysis): users per variation and, per metric, mean, percent change (lift), confidence interval, chance to beat control or p-value, plus health checks (sample ratio mismatch SRM, multiple exposures, power). Use after growthbook_get_experiment to decide a winner. Returns an error when no analysis has run; use growthbook_refresh_experiment_results first.

rows.dimension: Optional dimension to break results down by, e.g. exp:country or dim_...
rows.phase: Optional zero-based phase index (default: latest phase)

rows: Get one GrowthBook fact metric definition: numerator and denominator (fact table, column, filters), conversion window, capping, minimum sample size and percent change thresholds. Use after growthbook_list_fact_metrics.

Get one GrowthBook feature flag by key: default value, per-environment enabled state, targeting rules with conditions, saved groups, rollout coverage and linked experiments, prerequisites, and the published revision version. Use after growthbook_list_features.
Get GrowthBook code references for one feature flag: repositories, branches, files and lines that use the flag key. Use before removing a stale flag.

Check whether GrowthBook feature flags are stale (unused, fully rolled out, toggled off, no rules) overall and per environment, with the reason and what each environment evaluates to. Use for flag cleanup and tech-debt removal after growthbook_list_features.
Get one GrowthBook saved group (audience) including its condition or list of member values. Use after growthbook_list_saved_groups to see exactly who a targeting rule includes.

Get GrowthBook organization settings: feature flag key format (featureKeyExample, featureRegexValidator), statistics engine and thresholds, review requirements and kill switch confirmation. Use before growthbook_create_feature to follow the key format.
Get the status (running, success, error) of a GrowthBook experiment analysis snapshot. Use after growthbook_refresh_experiment_results to know when new experiment results are ready.
List GrowthBook targeting attributes (user properties such as id, country, deviceType) with data type, enum values and which one is used for hashing. Use to write or understand targeting conditions.

List the GrowthBook audit log (change history) for an entity type or one entity: who changed a feature flag, experiment or metric, what event, when, and why. Use to investigate who toggled a flag or changed an experiment.

rows.before: Optional cursor: nextCursor from the previous page, or an ISO date-time
rows.entity_id: Optional entity id (e.g. a feature flag key); omit for every entity of the type
rows.entity_type: Entity type, e.g. feature, experiment, metric, factMetric, savedGroup, sdkConnection, project, environment

rows: List GrowthBook code references: where feature flag keys appear in source code (repository, branch, file, line). Use for flag cleanup to find code still using a flag.

List GrowthBook data sources (warehouse connections) with type, identifier types and experiment assignment queries. Connection credentials are never returned. Use to understand where experiment exposure data comes from.
List GrowthBook environments (production, staging, dev) with whether each is production and its default flag state. Use to find environment ids before growthbook_toggle_feature.

List GrowthBook A/B test experiments with status (draft, running, stopped), variations, traffic split per phase, goal metrics, linked flag keys and the result summary (won, lost, inconclusive). Start here for GrowthBook experiment analysis and finding an experiment id. Paginated with limit/offset.

rows.archived: Optional boolean; true returns only archived experiments, false only active ones
rows.search: Optional search text (same syntax as the GrowthBook experiment list filter)
rows.status: Optional status filter: draft, running or stopped

rows: List GrowthBook fact metrics (the current metric type) used as experiment goals and guardrails: name, metric type (proportion, mean, ratio, quantile, retention), fact table and column, inverse flag. Use to resolve metric ids seen in experiments and results.
List GrowthBook fact tables: the warehouse SQL query, identifier types and columns that fact metrics are built from. Use to understand where a metric's data comes from.

List revisions (drafts and published versions) of one GrowthBook feature flag: version, status, author, comment, environments enabled and rules. Defaults to open drafts; pass status=published to see change history. Use after growthbook_get_feature to see what changed or what is pending review.

rows.status: Optional revision status: draft, published, discarded, approved, changes-requested, pending-review, pending-parent, or all-drafts (default: open drafts)

rows: List GrowthBook feature flags (features) with per-environment on/off state, default value, value type, tags and targeting rules (force, rollout, experiment). Start here for GrowthBook feature flag management, finding a flag key, and checking whether a flag or rollout is enabled in production. Paginated with limit/offset.

rows.archived: Optional boolean; true includes archived flags (default false)
rows.project_id: Optional GrowthBook project id (prj_...) from growthbook_list_projects

rows: List GrowthBook organization members (users) with name, email, role, teams and project roles. Use to resolve owner ids seen on flags and experiments.

List legacy GrowthBook SQL metrics (met_... ids, defined before fact metrics) with type (binomial, count, duration, revenue), data source and goal direction. Use when an experiment references a met_ metric id; prefer growthbook_list_fact_metrics for newer metrics.
List GrowthBook projects, which group feature flags, experiments and metrics and control access. Use to find the project_id filter for other GrowthBook tools.
List GrowthBook saved groups (reusable audiences and targeting segments: ID lists or conditions) referenced by feature flag rules and experiment targeting. Use to resolve grp_ ids seen in rules.

List GrowthBook SDK connections: which environment, projects and languages each client key serves, and whether payload encryption, remote evaluation or a proxy is on. Use to find which apps receive which feature flags. Encryption and proxy signing keys are never returned.
List GrowthBook segments (SQL or fact-table defined user subsets) that experiments can be analyzed against.

Publish a GrowthBook feature flag draft revision: its rules go live to every SDK in the environments they target. Only call this when a person has asked for the change to go live; show them the draft first (growthbook_list_feature_revisions). Gates GrowthBook enforces (required review, warnings, schema) come back as an error for a person to resolve; they are never bypassed. Returns pending_confirmation if the API key needs a person to confirm.

rows.comment: What goes live and why, recorded in the audit log

rows: Start a new GrowthBook experiment analysis snapshot, which runs the experiment's queries against the data warehouse and updates its results. Returns the snapshot id and status; poll growthbook_get_snapshot until status is success, then read growthbook_get_experiment_results. Costs warehouse compute.

rows.dimension: Optional dimension to break results down by, e.g. exp:country
rows.phase: Optional zero-based phase index (default: latest phase)

rows: Start a draft GrowthBook experiment: users matching its targeting are assigned to variations from the SDKs' next refresh, and feature drafts linked to it may be published with it. Only call this when a person has asked to launch. An incomplete launch checklist or a required approval comes back as an error for a person; it is never skipped.

Stop a running GrowthBook experiment and record its result (won, lost, inconclusive, dnf). With enable_temporary_rollout, one variation is served to all of its traffic. Use after growthbook_get_experiment_results.

rows.analysis: Optional markdown conclusion shown on the results page
rows.enable_temporary_rollout: Optional boolean: keep serving released_variation_id to all of the experiment's traffic
rows.released_variation_id: Variation id to serve to everyone, with enable_temporary_rollout
rows.results: won, lost, inconclusive or dnf (did not finish)
rows.winner_variation_id: Winning variation id (var_...), when results is won

rows: Turn a GrowthBook feature flag on or off (enable, disable, kill switch) in exactly one environment. Publishes a new revision; does not edit rules. If the API key requires confirmation, returns status pending_confirmation with a link for a person instead of applying it. Use after growthbook_get_feature to confirm the current state.

rows.enabled: true to turn the flag on in that environment, false to turn it off
rows.environment: Environment id to change (e.g. production); never defaults
rows.reason: Optional reason recorded in the GrowthBook audit log

rows: Change a GrowthBook experiment's settings (hypothesis, metrics, variations, phases, targeting, traffic split). On a running experiment the change is served from the SDKs' next refresh. Status changes go through growthbook_start_experiment and growthbook_stop_experiment.

rows.changes: JSON object with only the fields to change (same fields as growthbook_create_experiment)

rows: Change fields of one targeting rule of a GrowthBook feature flag in a draft revision (condition, value, coverage, environments, enabled, variations). The rule type cannot change. Nothing goes live until growthbook_publish_feature_revision. Get rule ids from growthbook_add_feature_rule or growthbook_list_feature_revisions.

rows.rule: JSON object with only the fields to change
